clue.text: Gore as President could turn out to be an economic disaster

indicators.note: the letters before it are said to turn out differently, so they are rearranged into something new

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of the hypothetical president's name and title

explanation.surface: A political jibe: had Al Gore become President, the economy would have collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Depression was the worldwide slump of the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Depression is the most famous example of a catastrophic economic slump.

clue.text: Time to visit our girls cheese rolling here?

definitions.text: Time to visit our girls cheese rolling here?

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the time letter joins the letters it calls on
rolling things tumble over, so these letters are tumbled into a new order

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An invitation to come along and watch the local girls chase a rolling cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the famous cheese-rolling race down Cooper's Hill takes place in Gloucestershire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloucestershire is the county in western England home to the annual Cooper's Hill cheese-rolling event.

clue.text: Base swine exposing Ionic descendants from Theban war dead

indicators.note: to expose is to strip off the covering, so the outer letters of the word are removed

blocks.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
the word with its first and last letters stripped

explanation.surface: A sneer at some lowly creatures uncovering classical Greek architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like an adjective insulting the swine, but it is the mathematical base e.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epigoni were the sons of the Seven against Thebes, who avenged their fathers killed in that war.

clue.text: Unappreciated, M Ryan's sometime co-star is bored by the French

indicators.note: something bored by another has that other drilled into it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: Tom Hanks, written as T Hanks to match M Ryan, starred with Meg Ryan in several films

explanation.surface: A gossip item about an actor whom Meg Ryan's old co-star found boring.
explanation.walkthrough: Writing Meg Ryan as M Ryan is the hint: her co-star Tom Hanks is wanted in the same initial-plus-surname form, which runs together as an ordinary word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thankless task or person goes unappreciated, receiving no gratitude for effort.

clue.text: Check out Hislop's organ when excited!

blocks.note: Ian Hislop edits the satirical magazine Private Eye, his organ or publication

explanation.surface: A cheeky instruction to look at a part of Ian Hislop's body when he is aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Hislop is a British TV satirist and editor of the magazine Private Eye; 'organ' means a publication, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye up someone is to look them over with interest, a colloquial way of saying check them out.

clue.text: Russian scheme to dominate alien world being explored

indicators.note: in a down entry, dominating means standing above, so the scheme sits on top of the alien

blocks.note: Red stands for Soviet or Russian

explanation.surface: A sinister Russian plot to dominate an alien planet under exploration.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars, nicknamed the red planet, is currently being explored by rovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is called the red planet for its rusty colour and is the world most actively explored by probes.

clue.text: Sting - intelligent and stylish

blocks.note: first meaning: to hurt with a sharp pain

explanation.surface: A tribute to the singer Sting as both clever and well dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting the musician is a distraction: three separate meanings of one word are listed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for painful smarting, and an adjective for both cleverness and a sharp, elegant appearance.

clue.text: Rapper that might get into Coke as a means to chill?

definitions.text: that might get into Coke as a means to chill?

blocks.note: first meaning: the stage name of an American hip-hop artist and actor

blocks.clueFragment: that might get into Coke as a means to chill?
blocks.note: second meaning: a frozen block dropped into a cola to cool it

explanation.surface: A musician who turns to cocaine to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at drugs and chilling out; read literally it is just something dropped into a glass of cola.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice Cube is a well-known rapper, and an ice cube is the frozen block used to cool a drink.

clue.text: Idea floated by last government leaves NHS disheartened

indicators.note: losing heart means the central part of the full expanded name is taken out

blocks.note: the abbreviation spelt out in full; its middle word is removed

explanation.surface: A political complaint that an idea from the previous government left the health service demoralised.
explanation.walkthrough: The Conservatives proposed bringing back a form of national service in their 2024 election campaign. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsory national service was a Conservative policy proposal in 2024, shortly before that government lost power.

clue.text: Wild herb Jones discovered outside Baltic capital

indicators.note: dis-covered means stripped of its cover, so the outer letters are dropped
one piece goes around the outside of the other

blocks.note: the name without its first and last letters
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: An explorer called Jones finds a wild herb beyond a Baltic city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' suggests finding something, but it means uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Origane is an old name for wild marjoram, or oregano, a herb growing wild.

clue.text: Face shock therapy, in a manner of speaking

explanation.surface: An instruction to confront electroconvulsive treatment, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' reads as a throwaway idiom, but its last words are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional variety of a language, a particular way of speaking.

clue.text: Wedge of cheese for starters served with German wine

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: hock is a white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A slice of cheese offered as a first course with a glass of Rhine wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wedge of cheese' is a natural phrase, but only 'Wedge' defines. Hock is the British name for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A chock is a block or wedge placed against a wheel to stop it moving.

clue.text: Mostly well-mannered dude taking over university committee

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter goes
taking something over means taking it in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: informal for a man or mate

explanation.surface: A mostly polite young man taking charge of a university committee.
explanation.definitionFit: The Politburo was the chief policy-making committee of a Communist party, as in the Soviet Union.

clue.text: Crassly name-drops one replacing old web designer

indicators.note: one thing replacing another takes its spot, so a letter is swapped out
done crassly means clumsily, so the letters end up in a mess

explanation.surface: Someone vulgarly dropping names to replace an old designer of websites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Web designer' sounds like a website developer; it is the superhero who spins webs.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider-Man is the comic-book hero who shoots and swings on webs of his own making.

clue.text: 5 sick in Eastern European port

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the pair of letters that follow

blocks.note: the answer to 5 Down is the red planet, Mars

explanation.surface: Someone falls ill in a port somewhere in Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern European port' suggests Gdansk or Odessa, but the port is on the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Marseille is France's largest seaport, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Goddess has The King of Spain wearing absolutely nothing

indicators.note: what is worn goes around the wearer, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: sweet FA is British slang for absolutely nothing

explanation.surface: A goddess and the Spanish king are both stark naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing absolutely nothing' paints a naked king; the king is in fact inside FA, from 'sweet FA', British slang meaning nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse goddess of love and fertility.

clue.text: Completed almost all Sildenafil supply

indicators.note: almost all of the word is used, so one letter is dropped
read as the adverb of supple, these letters are bent freely into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A pharmacy has finished off nearly all its stock of the drug sold as Viagra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun about stock, but read as 'supple-ly' it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Finalised means brought to a finished, settled state, as a completed deal is.

clue.text: Prosecute retired doctor arrested, put on board coach

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the word is read from the end
an arrested person is held, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: to sue is to take legal action
Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree

explanation.surface: A retired doctor is arrested, prosecuted and put on a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired doctor' reads as a pensioner medic, but 'retired' belongs to the prosecuting word.
explanation.definitionFit: To embus is a military term for loading troops onto a bus or vehicle.

clue.text: Favour nurse in suit

indicators.note: one piece placed within the other

explanation.surface: Asking a favour of a nurse wearing a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: The nurse abbreviation goes after the first letter of the five-letter verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is an advantage or favour done for someone.

clue.text: Nitre swirling around - it's a problem for the eyes

indicators.note: swirling things spin about, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that saltpetre swirling in the air irritates the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinitis is inflammation of the retina, a medical condition affecting the eyes.

clue.text: Awful driver crossing street sustained by American snack

indicators.note: to cross something here is to straddle it, so one piece spans the other
in a down entry, being sustained means being held up from below, so the last piece goes underneath

blocks.note: Mr Toad of The Wind in the Willows, a notoriously reckless motorist

explanation.surface: A bad driver crosses the road, kept going by an American snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A tostada is a Mexican snack of a fried tortilla topped with beans, meat and so on.

clue.text: Ageing banker in Paris exuding Gucci's latest perfume

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is the last one written
exuding means giving off, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a banker is a river, one with banks; this one flows through Paris
last letter of the brand name

explanation.surface: An elderly Parisian financier reeking of Gucci's newest fragrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' suggests a financier; in crosswords it can mean a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Senescent describes something growing old, deteriorating with age.

clue.text: Country hospital taking care of upper-class duke

indicators.note: taking care of someone means taking them in, so one piece holds the others

blocks.note: U means upper-class in British usage

explanation.surface: A rural hospital caring for an aristocratic duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country hospital' reads as one phrase, but 'Country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a nation in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Licence to Kill Bill initially forbidden

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so that piece comes first

blocks.note: James Bond's 00 prefix grants a licence to kill

explanation.surface: Two film titles, Licence to Kill and Kill Bill, run together as if banned.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as Bond and Tarantino film titles; 'Kill Bill' is split across two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is socially prohibited, ruled out by custom.

clue.text: Producer of light sailing dinghy

blocks.note: first meaning: a device emitting a concentrated beam
second meaning: a popular class of single-handed racing boat

explanation.surface: A maker of lightweight sailing boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser emits an intense beam, and the Laser is an Olympic single-handed dinghy class.

clue.text: Popular guerrilla leader is a non-believer

blocks.note: Fidel Castro led the Cuban guerrilla revolution

explanation.surface: A popular rebel commander declares himself an atheist.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is someone without religious faith, especially from another religion's viewpoint.

clue.text: Back in Delhi, Tam sabotaged cash crop

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow
going back means reading from the end towards the start

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: On returning to Delhi, someone named Tam wrecked a profitable harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Basmati rice is grown for sale and export in India and Pakistan, a crop raised for money.

clue.text: Controversially re-elected on anti European peace initiative

indicators.note: a controversial result is disputed and overturned, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician wins a disputed re-election on an anti-European platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anti European' looks like a single phrase; 'European' actually belongs with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Entente Cordiale was the 1904 agreement settling Anglo-French differences and improving relations.
